title: Features and labels
summary: A feature is an input measurement. A label is the known answer in a teaching example. Scikit-learn usually expects a table of feature rows.
introduction: A feature is an input measurement. A label is the known answer in a teaching example. Scikit-learn usually expects a table of feature rows. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A feature is an input measurement. A label is the known answer in a teaching example. Scikit-learn usually expects a table of feature rows.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Use Python with scikit-learn installed in a separate environment. These lessons need no remote AI service or secret key. They do not run in the browser playground.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Scikit-learn. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.
The output is 4 4. Each one-value feature row has one matching class label. The labels are fictional groups.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add one row and its matching label.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not give a different number of feature rows and labels.
For more detail later, use this [Scikit-learn further reading](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/getting_started.html).
